questions.question: Which of the following fuels is the largest contributor to the generation of electricity in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Coal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Three fuels—coal, oil, and solid biomass**—provide more than 80% of India's energy requirements.
 
• Coal, which still dominates the energy mix, has fostered the development of industry and the **generation of electricity. **
 
• In the previous four decades, **India's commercial primary energy consumption **has increased by nearly 700%. India currently consumes roughly **350 kgoe/year of commercial primary energy** per person, which is far less than that of wealthy nations.
 
• **Around 75% of the total power generated** is produced by coal-fired thermal power plants, which also produce the majority of electricity. The Central Electricity Authority said that **India generated 103.66 billion units of electricity** in December of 2020.
 
• According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, **coal, nuclear power, and natural gas **made up the majority of the country's electrical generation in 2020.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gujarat (43.6 GW), Maharashtra (42.3 GW), and Tamil Nadu (36.3 GW) **are the top three states in terms of electricity generation capacity, however Karnataka is the top s**tate in terms of renewable energy capacity.**
 
• **According to a state-by-state report** provided by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Rajasthan has the highest installed solar energy capacity in India, with 7737.95MW (MNRE).
 
• India's top solar energy producer is the **southwestern state of Karnataka**. With a roughly 7,100MW total installed solar power capacity.

questions.question: Which of the following places has a nuclear power plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaiga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Kaiga Atomic Power Station (KAPS) is operated by the state-run Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL).
 
• Kaiga Site is located on Kadra Reservoir on Kali river in Uttar Kannada district in the state of Karnataka.
 
• The plant services India's southern grid and provides power to five states (Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Pondicherry).
 
• It consists of two Stations-
 
 
• Kaiga Generating Station (KGS) 1 & 2 – Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (2 x 220 MWe PHWR)
 
• Kaiga Generating Station (KGS) 3 & 4 – Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (2 x 220 MWe PHWR)
 
 
 
• Hence Kaiga has four indigenously developed Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors of 220 MW each fuelled by domestic fuel.
 
• The first unit of the project, meanwhile, set a world record on December 10, 2018, operating uninterrupted for more than 940 days held by Heysham-Unit 2 of the United Kingdom, and in 2019 it has set a new benchmark of 962 days of uninterrupted operation and has now been shut down for maintenance.

questions.question: Where is the Kudremukh iron ore mine located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

__
 
• **KIOCL Limited (formerly Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Limited) is a Government of India Undertaking established in the year 1976 and is operating Iron Ore Pellet Plant and Pig Iron Plant at Mangalore, Panambur, Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Limited **is a state-owned iron ore producer with its headquarters and administrative activities in Bangalore, Karnataka.

 
 
• It has a pelletization plant at Mangalore and an iron ore mine located in Kudremukh National Park, Chikmagalur district, Karnataka.
 
• It is owned by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India.
 
• Kudremukh mine is one of the largest iron ore mines in the world.
 
• The plant was shut down in 2011 but in 2014 the plant resumed production and export of pellets run on ores supplied by NMDC Ltd.
 
• There were plans to resume captive mining operations in 2017, now at Sanduru in Bellary district.
 
• The pellets have been shipped to countries such as China, Iran, Japan and Taiwan.
 
• Kudremukh will become the world's largest iron ore-producing mine within five years.

questions.question: Jute is also known as ______ fibre.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**golden**__.

__
 
• **Jute **is also known as **golden fibre**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• A material that is composed of thin and continuous strands is known as** fibre.**
 
• Plant fibers are elongated most commonly sclerenchyma supportive plant cells with thick cellulose walls with a well-organized structure.
 
• Fibre can be of** two types.**
 
 
• Natural fibre
 
• Synthetic fibre
 
 
 
• The fibres which are obtained from plants and animals are known as natural fibres whereas synthetic fibres are man-made fibres; most of them are prepared from raw materials (petroleum) called petrochemicals.
 
• **Examples** of **natural fibres** are **cotton and jute **whereas examples of **synthetic fibres** are: **nylon, polyester.**
 
• **Jute fibre**
 
 
• **​Jute fibre** is obtained only from the **stem** of the** jute plants.**
 
• It is mainly grown in the rainy season.
 
• Jute mainly grows in regions having **alluvial soil** which is found in the delta regions of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers.
 
• In India, jute is basically grown in the states of Bihar, West Bengal and Assam.
 
• Jute is sometimes also called the **golden fibre**.
 
• It is **soft, shiny and long fibre** with a **silky texture.**
 
• The jute plant is about 3 meters in height and bears yellow flowers in a few months.
 
• During this time, the liquid skin moves out to separate the fibre and this process is known as retting.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Diamond is the hardest material on the earth and it is a solid form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic.

 Platinum is a chemical element with the symbol Pt and atomic number 78. It is a dense, malleable, ductile, highly unreactive, precious, silverish-white transition metal.
 
 

 **Silver**
 Silver is a chemical element with the symbol Ag and atomic number 47. A soft, white, lustrous transition metal, exhibits the highest electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and reflectivity of any metal.

questions.question: The mineral called carnotite is an important source of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__Uranium__.

__
 
• Carnotite is a **potassium** uranium vanadate **radioactive** mineral with the **chemical** formula **K₂(UO₂)₂(VO₄)₂·3H₂O**.
 
• Pure carnotite contains about** 53** **percent uranium**, **12** **percent vanadium**, and trace amounts of **radium**.
 
• It is of **secondary** origin, having been formed by alteration of primary **uranium-vanadium** minerals.
 
• It occurs chiefly with **tyuyamunite** in **sandstone **either disseminated or locally as small pure masses, particularly around **fossil** wood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46bc3582c4d8ff7880d2ffc7bf4aaa0ec19bedb406157a551233cdc970585b51.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Carnotite has provided most of the **uranium** production from **secondary** deposits it is also mined for **vanadium** and **radium** from **1911** to **1923.**
 
• After **World War II,** it was mined extensively in the **U.S.** for** uranium**. The greatest known** concentration** of **carnotite **deposits is in the **western U.S**.

• Tertiary coal is found in** the rocks of the Oligocene period of the Tertiary Era.**
 
• Tertiary coal fields share only **1% of the coal production of India.**
 
• Tertiary coal is also known as **'brown coal'.**
 
• Tertiary coal** contributes** only about **two per cent of the total coal production **of the country.

• Coal is the foremost power resources in India and is the most abundantly available fossil fuel.
 
• India is highly dependent on coal for meeting its commercial energy requirements. 
 
• Coal is found in **a variety of forms depending on the degrees of compression and the depth and time of burial.**
 
• **Types of Coal :**
 
 
• **Anthracite** (more than 80% carbon content):
 
 
• In India, it is found only in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Bituminous** (60 to 80 % Carbon Content):
 
 
• It is the second-best quality of coal.
 
• It is the most popular coal in commercial use.
 
 
 
• ** Peat **(less than 40% carbon content)
 
• ** Lignite :**
 
 
• ** **It is low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content.
 
 
 
• The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli in Tamil Nadu and are used for the generation of electricity.
 
 
 
 
 
• **The Damodar Valley Coalfield** is the **largest coalfield in India **that extended to Jharkhand and West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following gas causes explosion in coal mines?
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Methane.**__

__**There are two main types of coal mine explosions:**__

__
 
• **Methane **__explosions occur when methane gas from mining is built up and cannot escape because of high pressure.
 
• Coal dust is also highly inflammable in nature and causes explosions.

 
 

 
 
Coal

 
 
 
 Specifications

 
 
 

 
 
Anthracite

 
 
 
 
• The highest rank of coal. It is a hard, brittle, and black lustrous coal, often referred to as hard coal, containing a high percentage of fixed carbon and a low percentage of volatile matter.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Lignite

 
 
 
 
• Lignite coal, brown coal, is the lowest grade coal with the least concentration of carbon
 
 
 
 

 
 
Bituminous

 
 
 
 
• Bituminous coal is middle-rank coal between sub-bituminous and anthracite.
 
• Bituminous usually has a high heating (Btu) value and is the most common type of coal used in electricity generation.
 
• Bituminous coal appears shiny and smooth when you first see it but look closer and you may see it has layers.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Peat

 
 
 
 
• Peat is not actually coal, but rather the precursor to coal.
 
• Peat is a soft organic material consisting of partly decayed plant and, in some cases, deposited mineral matter.
 
• When peat is placed under high pressure and heat, it becomes coal.

questions.question: As of January 2021, more than 93% of India’s chromite resources were located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chromite **is the single commercially viable ore of chromium which is chemically known as** iron chromium oxide**. 
 
• More than **93 percent** of the Chromite resources in India are found in **Sukinda valley in Cuttack **and **Jajapur in Odisha. **
 
• Minor deposits are spread over **Manipur, Nagaland, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu**, and **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a steel-grey, lustrous, hard, and brittle metal which takes a high polish, resists tarnishing, and has a high melting point.
 
• The properties of chromium that make it most versatile and indispensable are its resistance to corrosion, oxidation, and wear.
 
• Chromium is an important alloying metal. It is used in the manufacture of alloys along with other metals, such as nickel, cobalt, copper, etc.
 
• It is also used in many other metallurgical, refractories, and chemical industries.
